correctness.rationale: Write the row probabilities for 00, 10, 01, 11 as a=1−2p+q, b=p−q, b and d=q. Rank is below two exactly when all nonzero rows occupy at most one direction. Inclusion–exclusion yields F_n=2(a+b)^n+(a+d)^n−2a^n, with the common intersection the all-zero sample. At fixed p the derivative in q is 2n[(a+q)^(n−1)−a^(n−1)], positive at any feasible q>0, so the smallest feasible q is uniquely optimal. Independently, if a>0, replacing zeros independently by uniform nonzero row types preserves equality of the two marginals, never destroys rank, and strictly improves recovery on the all-zero event. Hence the global optimum has a=0. On that edge strict convexity of x^n equalizes the three masses at 1/3, giving p=2/3, q=1/3 and failure 3^(1−n) for all n≥2. The iid-row strong law gives Gram/n with diagonal p and off-diagonal q, hence minimum eigenvalue b≤1/2 with equality exactly when a=d=0. Substitution gives the two condition-number limits and failure probabilities, and at p=2/3, q=p² the leading failure term (5/9)^n gives ratio asymptotic to (5/3)^n/3.
residual_risks: All conclusions use identical independent rows and real rank. The zero-atom replacement is only for the optimization over varying p, not a fixed-input rounding scheme.
